uncited: Unlike direct integration methods that trace paths per pixel, these methods store photon interactions in spatial structures and estimate incident radiance at query points using kernel density estimation or explicit summation [S2].

What sets this family apart from its siblings is the specific use of stored photon data (points, beams, or surfaces) to approximate the integral of the radiance transfer equation, differing from the explicit path tracing of [Compute Shader Photon Integration](2111-compute-shader-photon-integration.md) and the boundary-segment sampling of [Grid-based Importance Sampling for Boundary Segments](7643-grid-based-importance-sampling-for-boundary-segments.md).
where $\tau$ is the optical depth (integrated extinction) [S3].
This technique allows for the simulation of complex light transport paths within participating media without requiring full path tracing for every pixel.
The method was developed to address the high variance and computational cost of direct integration methods for multiple scattering in complex media.
It has since been extended to photon beams and various density estimation techniques to improve efficiency and accuracy in rendering participating media.
